summary: Phase 5 (FR-14): IM3 auth server.ts now delegates to core-auth request-guards. All 11 public function signatures preserved with identical parameter types and return types. Consumers (7 route handlers) receive SessionClaims | Response with same status codes (401/403/503) and JSON body shape { error: msg }. NextResponse import removed; core-auth uses native Response which satisfies all existing instanceof Response checks. Phase 7 (FR-17/19/20): generator-registry.test.ts and games-exports.test.ts changes are purely additive to test files; no production code modified. FR-20 lessons-learned entry captures the test-integrity anti-pattern. Phase 8 (FR-15): --db and --symbol junk files deleted; .gitignore guards /--db, /--symbol, and *-cli-arg-junk glob. No legitimate tracked files match the new gitignore patterns. All IM3 auth tests pass (61/61). study-hub-core tests pass (10/10). Pre-existing math-content test failures (17 tests) unchanged — out of scope per spec.

nonblocking_findings.description: core-auth response builders use new Response(JSON.stringify(...)) instead of NextResponse.json(). Both produce identical { error: msg } JSON body and status codes, and both satisfy instanceof Response. However, the Content-Type header is now set explicitly via headers option rather than via NextResponse internals. This is semantically equivalent but worth noting for completeness.

The *-cli-arg-junk glob pattern in .gitignore has no leading / prefix, so it applies recursively across all subdirectories. While no current files match and the suffix is specific, this is broader than the /--db and /--symbol entries which are root-only. Consider narrowing to /*-cli-arg-junk if junk files are only created at the repo root.
